const WORKLOAD = {"name":"Legal contract review","kind":"text","task":"Answer one question about a commercial contract, from the contract text alone.","answer_instruction":"You are reviewing a commercial contract. Answer the question in ONE short sentence. State the figure or provision directly. Do not explain your reasoning.","contract":"MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement ("Agreement") is entered into as of 1 March 2026 (the
"Effective Date") between:

  Kestrel Data Oy, a company registered in Helsinki, Finland ("Supplier"); and
  Pinewright Retail GmbH, a company registered in Hamburg, Germany ("Customer").

ALL PARTIES, CLAUSES, FIGURES AND CIRCUMSTANCES IN THIS DOCUMENT ARE FICTIONAL. It is
synthetic test data written for a benchmarking exercise. It is not legal advice, it models
no real agreement, and it names no real company.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1.1 "Services" means the data processing and analytics services described in Schedule A.

1.2 "Personal Data" has the meaning given in Article 4(1) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679
    ("GDPR").

1.3 "Service Credit" means the remedy set out in Clause 7.

1.4 "Affiliate" means any entity controlling, controlled by, or under common control with
    a party, where "control" means direct or indirect ownership of more than fifty per cent
    (50%) of the voting securities.

1.5 Headings are for convenience only and do not affect interpretation.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. TERM
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

2.1 This Agreement commences on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of
    twenty-four (24) months (the "Initial Term"), expiring on 28 February 2028.

2.2 Following the Initial Term, this Agreement renews automatically for successive periods
    of twelve (12) months (each a "Renewal Term"), unless either party gives written notice
    of non-renewal not less than ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term.

2.3 Expiry or termination of this Agreement does not affect any provision that is intended
    to survive, including Clauses 10, 12 and 15.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. TERMINATION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

3.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving the other party not
    less than sixty (60) days' written notice, provided that the Customer may not serve
    such notice before the first anniversary of the Effective Date.

3.2 Either party may terminate this Agreement immediately on written notice if the other
    party commits a material breach and fails to cure that breach within thirty (30) days
    of receiving written notice describing it.

3.3 Either party may terminate immediately if the other becomes insolvent, enters
    administration, or ceases to carry on business.

3.4 Termination for any reason does not relieve the Customer of its obligation to pay all
    fees accrued up to the effective date of termination.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. FEES AND PAYMENT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

4.1 The Customer shall pay a recurring fee of EUR 18,000 per calendar month for the
    Services, invoiced monthly in advance.

4.2 All invoices are payable within forty-five (45) days of the invoice date.

4.3 Overdue amounts accrue interest at the rate of one and a half per cent (1.5%) per month,
    calculated from the due date until payment is received in full.

4.4 Fees are exclusive of value added tax and any other applicable taxes, which the
    Customer shall pay in addition.

4.5 All amounts are stated and payable in euro (EUR).

4.6 The Customer shall reimburse the Supplier for pre-approved travel and subsistence costs
    incurred in the performance of the Services, at cost, supported by receipts.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. SUPPLIER OBLIGATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

5.1 The Supplier shall perform the Services with reasonable skill and care and in
    accordance with Schedule A.

5.2 The Supplier shall provide the Services in accordance with the service levels set out
    in Clause 7.

5.3 The Supplier shall appoint a named service manager and shall make that person available
    to the Customer for a monthly review meeting.

5.4 The Supplier shall maintain a documented business continuity and disaster recovery plan,
    and shall test that plan not less than once every twelve (12) months.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. CUSTOMER OBLIGATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

6.1 The Customer shall provide the Supplier with timely access to the systems, data and
    personnel reasonably required for the performance of the Services.

6.2 The Customer shall ensure that it has a lawful basis for any Personal Data it transfers
    to the Supplier for processing.

6.3 The Customer shall not use the Services in a manner that is unlawful or that infringes
    the rights of any third party.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. SERVICE LEVELS AND SERVICE CREDITS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

7.1 The Supplier shall make the Services available at a monthly availability of not less
    than ninety-nine point nine per cent (99.9%), measured in accordance with Schedule B.

7.2 Where monthly availability falls below the commitment in Clause 7.1, the Customer is
    entitled to a Service Credit of ten per cent (10%) of the monthly fee for each full
    zero point one per cent (0.1%) by which availability falls short.

7.3 The aggregate Service Credit in any single calendar month shall not exceed thirty per
    cent (30%) of the monthly fee for that month.

7.4 Service Credits are the Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for any failure to meet
    the service levels in this Clause 7.

7.5 The Customer must claim a Service Credit within thirty (30) days of the end of the
    calendar month in which the shortfall occurred. Claims made after that period are
    void.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. LIABILITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

8.1 Neither party excludes or limits its liability for death or personal injury caused by
    negligence, for fraud or fraudulent misrepresentation, or for any other liability that
    cannot lawfully be limited.

8.2 Subject to Clause 8.1, the total aggregate liability of each party arising out of or in
    connection with this Agreement is limited to the total fees paid or payable by the
    Customer in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the
    claim.

8.3 The limitation in Clause 8.2 does NOT apply to liability arising from:

    (a) a breach by the Supplier of Clause 12 (Data Protection); or
    (b) the Supplier's indemnity obligations under Clause 9.1.

8.4 The liability of the Supplier under Clause 9.1 (intellectual property indemnity) is
    instead limited to twice (2x) the amount calculated under Clause 8.2.

8.5 Neither party is liable for loss of profit, loss of revenue, loss of anticipated
    savings, or any indirect or consequential loss, whether arising in contract, tort
    (including negligence) or otherwise.

8.6 The Customer shall not make any claim under this Agreement more than twenty-four (24)
    months after the date on which it became aware, or ought reasonably to have become
    aware, of the circumstances giving rise to the claim.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
9. INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

9.1 The Supplier shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the Customer against any claim
    that the Services, as provided by the Supplier and used by the Customer in accordance
    with this Agreement, infringe any intellectual property right of a third party.

9.2 Each party retains all right, title and interest in its own pre-existing intellectual
    property.

9.3 The Customer grants the Supplier a non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to use the
    Customer's data solely to the extent necessary to perform the Services.

9.4 All intellectual property created by the Supplier in the course of performing the
    Services vests in the Supplier.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
10. CONFIDENTIALITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

10.1 Each party shall keep confidential all Confidential Information of the other party and
     shall not disclose it except as permitted by this Clause 10.

10.2 Confidentiality obligations continue for five (5) years after the date of disclosure,
     and indefinitely in respect of trade secrets.

10.3 Disclosure is permitted where required by law, provided the disclosing party gives the
     other party prompt notice where lawfully able to do so.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
11. INSURANCE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

11.1 The Supplier shall maintain professional indemnity insurance with a limit of not less
     than EUR 5,000,000 per claim, and public liability insurance with a limit of not less
     than EUR 2,000,000 per claim.

11.2 The Supplier shall provide evidence of cover on request, and shall give the Customer
     thirty (30) days' notice of any material reduction in cover.

11.3 The Customer shall maintain cyber liability insurance with a limit of not less than
     EUR 3,000,000 per claim.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
12. DATA PROTECTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

12.1 The parties shall comply with all applicable data protection law, including the GDPR.

12.2 The Supplier shall process Personal Data only on the documented instructions of the
     Customer, and shall not process it for its own purposes.

12.3 The Supplier shall implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to
     ensure a level of security appropriate to the risk.

12.4 The Supplier shall notify the Customer without undue delay, and in any event within
     seventy-two (72) hours, of becoming aware of a Personal Data Breach affecting Personal
     Data processed under this Agreement.

12.5 The Customer authorises the Supplier to engage the subprocessors listed in Schedule C.
     The Supplier shall give the Customer not less than thirty (30) days' written notice
     before adding or replacing any subprocessor, during which the Customer may object on
     reasonable data protection grounds.

12.6 Where the Customer objects under Clause 12.5 and the parties cannot resolve the
     objection within thirty (30) days, the Customer may terminate this Agreement on thirty
     (30) days' written notice.

12.7 The Supplier shall assist the Customer in responding to data subject requests, and
     shall provide such assistance within five (5) business days of a written request.

12.8 On termination, the Supplier shall delete or return all Personal Data within sixty (60)
     days, at the Customer's choice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
13. ASSIGNMENT AND SUBCONTRACTING
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

13.1 Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent
     of the other party, except to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger or sale of
     substantially all of its assets.

13.2 The Supplier remains fully liable for the acts and omissions of its subprocessors and
     subcontractors.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
14. AUDIT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

14.1 The Customer may audit the Supplier's compliance with this Agreement not more than once
     in any twelve (12) month period, on not less than thirty (30) days' written notice.

14.2 The Customer may audit more frequently where required by a regulator or following a
     Personal Data Breach.

14.3 Audits shall be conducted during business hours and shall not unreasonably interfere
     with the Supplier's operations.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
15. GOVERNING LAW AND DISPUTE RESOLUTION
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

15.1 This Agreement is governed by the laws of Finland, excluding its conflict of laws
     rules.

15.2 Any dispute arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall be finally
     settled by arbitration in Helsinki, Finland, before a single arbitrator, in accordance
     with the Arbitration Rules of the Finland Chamber of Commerce.

15.3 The language of the arbitration shall be English.

15.4 Nothing in this Clause prevents either party from seeking urgent injunctive relief from
     a court of competent jurisdiction.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
16. GENERAL
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

16.1 This Agreement, together with its Schedules, constitutes the entire agreement between
     the parties and supersedes all prior discussions and representations.

16.2 No variation of this Agreement is effective unless made in writing and signed by both
     parties.

16.3 No failure or delay in exercising a right operates as a waiver of that right.

16.4 If any provision is found to be invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions
     continue in full force.

16.5 Notices under this Agreement shall be in writing and sent by hand, by courier, or by
     email with confirmed receipt, to the addresses set out in Schedule D.

16.6 Nothing in this Agreement creates a partnership, joint venture or relationship of
     agency between the parties.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEDULE A - SERVICES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

A.1 Ingestion of the Customer's transactional data into the Supplier's analytics platform.

A.2 Daily reconciliation reporting, delivered by 07:00 CET on the following business day.

A.3 A monthly analytics review meeting.

A.4 Second-line support during business hours (08:00-18:00 CET, Monday to Friday, excluding
    Finnish public holidays).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEDULE B - AVAILABILITY MEASUREMENT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

B.1 Availability is calculated monthly as (Total Minutes - Excluded Minutes - Downtime
    Minutes) / (Total Minutes - Excluded Minutes) x 100.

B.2 "Excluded Minutes" means minutes lost to scheduled maintenance notified at least
    seventy-two (72) hours in advance, and minutes lost to force majeure.

B.3 Scheduled maintenance is permitted between 22:00 and 02:00 CET.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEDULE C - AUTHORISED SUBPROCESSORS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

C.1 Aurelia Cloud Services Ltd (infrastructure hosting, Ireland)

C.2 Brightpath Monitoring Oy (application monitoring, Finland)

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
SCHEDULE D - NOTICE ADDRESSES
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Supplier: legal@kestrel-data.example, or Kestrel Data Oy, Aleksanterinkatu 00, Helsinki.

Customer: legal@pinewright-retail.example, or Pinewright Retail GmbH, Beispielstrasse 00,
Hamburg.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
END OF AGREEMENT
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

const all = $input.all();
let orCatalog = null;
let hfCatalog = null;
for (const it of all) {
  const d = it.json;
  const arr = Array.isArray(d) ? d : (d && d.data ? d.data : []);
  if (!arr.length) continue;
  const first = arr[0];
  if (first && first.providers) hfCatalog = arr;
  else if (first && first.pricing && typeof first.pricing.prompt === "string") orCatalog = arr;
}
const perM = function (s) {
  return s === undefined || s === null || s === "" ? null : Number(s) * 1e6;
};
const orBySlug = {};
for (const m of (orCatalog || [])) orBySlug[m.id] = m;
const hfBySlug = {};
for (const m of (hfCatalog || [])) hfBySlug[m.id] = m;

function lookup(c) {
  if (c.source === "openrouter") {
    const m = orBySlug[c.slug];
    if (!m) return { ok: false, reason: "not in the OpenRouter catalogue (renamed or withdrawn)" };
    const p = m.pricing || {};
    const tier = (p.overrides || [])[0] || null;
    return {
      ok: true, catalogued: true, context_length: m.context_length,
      input_per_m: perM(p.prompt), output_per_m: perM(p.completion),
      cache_read_per_m: perM(p.input_cache_read),
      tier_min_prompt_tokens: tier ? tier.min_prompt_tokens : null,
      tier_input_per_m: tier ? perM(tier.prompt) : null,
      output_modalities: (m.architecture && m.architecture.output_modalities) || null,
      providers_live: null,
    };
  }
  const m = hfBySlug[c.slug];
  if (!m) return { ok: false, reason: "not in the HF router catalogue" };
  const live = (m.providers || []).filter(function (p) { return p.status === "live"; });
  const chosen = live.filter(function (p) { return p.provider === c.provider; })[0] || live[0];
  if (!chosen) return { ok: false, reason: "no live provider publishes this model" };
  const pr = chosen.pricing || {};
  return {
    ok: true, catalogued: true, provider: chosen.provider, context_length: chosen.context_length,
    input_per_m: pr.input == null ? null : Number(pr.input),
    output_per_m: pr.output == null ? null : Number(pr.output),
    cache_read_per_m: null, tier_min_prompt_tokens: null, tier_input_per_m: null,
    output_modalities: ["text"], providers_live: live.length,
  };
}

const out = [];
const validationNotes = [];
for (const c of WORKLOAD.candidates) {
  const info = lookup(c);
  if (!info.ok) {
    validationNotes.push(c.name + ": " + info.reason);
    continue;
  }
  if (info.output_modalities && info.output_modalities.indexOf("text") === -1) {
    validationNotes.push(c.name + ": catalogue says it does not output text");
    continue;
  }
  for (const g of WORKLOAD.golden_set) {
    const messages = [
      { role: "system", content: WORKLOAD.answer_instruction },
      { role: "user", content: "CONTRACT:
" + WORKLOAD.contract + "

QUESTION: " + g.question },
    ];
    out.push({ json: {
      candidate: c.name, slug: c.slug, source: c.source, route: c.route,
      provider: info.provider || c.provider || null, incumbent: c.incumbent,
      question_id: g.id, question_kind: g.kind, expected: g.expected,
      accept: g.accept || [], reject: g.reject || [],
      validation: info, validation_notes: validationNotes,
      url: c.source === "openrouter" ? WORKLOAD.endpoints.openrouter : WORKLOAD.endpoints.huggingface,
      body: { model: c.slug, messages: messages, max_tokens: 400, temperature: 0 },
    }});
  }
}
if (!out.length) throw new Error("no candidate passed validation: " + validationNotes.join("; "));
return out;

parameters.content:
Step 1 - requirements gate, before price.

Both catalogues are fetched with raw HTTP Request nodes, normalised to USD per 1M tokens in one Code node, and the shortlist is validated against what the catalogues actually publish. Then one item is created per candidate per golden-set question.

nodes.name: Note: Step 1 - requirements gate, before price

parameters.content:
Step 2 - measure, don't multiply.

Every call is made for real and timed to the last byte. Quality is scored by rules against known answers: correct share, p50/p95 latency, and a hallucination flag with the answer attached. No LLM judge.

Keys are read from n8n Variables (OPENROUTER_API_KEY, HF_TOKEN), or from the environment on a self-hosted instance with N8N_BLOCK_ENV_ACCESS_IN_NODE=false. Nothing secret is in this file.

Steps 3 and 4 - price the survivors, then show the gap.

Five price mechanics, three procurement routes, and the buyer's estimate against the measurement with each error named. Route C stays an estimate and is never given a monthly figure beside the two quoted routes.
